sentences: September 21, 2022 last edits 9/26 Earlier, I wrote of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) "Russian forces are accused of militarizing the site by basing forces there (seems undeniably true to some degree) and launching attacks from there (not so sure, but troubling if so - I'll have some to say on this in another post)." This is that post.

On the night of March 3/4, the plant was already occupied - debatably "militarized" - by a Ukrainian "assigned military unit." Russian attacks in and around the plant were in response to attacks by those forces.

Wall Street Journal, July 5: Russian Army Turns Ukraine’s Largest Nuclear Plant Into a Military Base ( archived ) Russian forces at the plant "have in recent weeks deployed heavy artillery batteries and laid anti-personnel mines along the shores of the reservoir whose water cools its six reactors, according to workers, residents, Ukrainian officials, and diplomats.

Russian forces deployed a Smerch artillery vehicle last month in the shadow of the 5.7 gigawatt complex’s striped chimneys, adding to the grad rocket launchers, tanks and personnel carriers." But there were no link or supports for the Smerch claim, and I haven't seen anything else in support.
In review: Russian forces are seen firing tank cannons, RPGs and more in many directions, many times.
And then we see and hear about attacks against the plant as the Russians allegedly shelled themselves in response.

Russia's explanation for the forces at the plant are reflected in Ambassador Ulyanov's comments (continued): "Russian law enforcement agencies at the ZNPP are represented only by units of Rosgvardia (an analogue of the French gendarmes and Italian carabinieri) and specialists from the troops of radiation, chemical and biological protection (RCBP).
StopFake called out "Russian propagandists" for claiming Ukraine had shelled the plant in this attack.

That was "fake" because they targeted Russian equipment, not the plant, and the attack "did not take place in the immediate territory of the ZNPP." This launcher is on the ZNPP grounds, by most definitions, but near the eastern perimeter.
But a photo with the article shows "A Russian tank outside Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in a picture released mid-March." It's parked and covered, but present.

Otherwise, satellite and drone views show just armored personnel carriers (APCs) and supply trucks, and a military tent camp that was attacked on July 20 ( video ) or the 19th by other reports ( CNN ), in the area marked C on the top map.
It's not visibly clear if they're all soldiers or if they might include civilian specialists or others.
Add 9/26: One report I found traces a likely connection: "Russia on Wednesday (20 July) accused Ukraine of targetting a nuclear power station in the Zaporizhzhia region using drones.
Energoatom alleged that Russian forces were demanding access to the machine halls of three reactors for storing tanks and equipment there, reported Reuters.
However, the company also did not comment on the drone attack by Ukrainian forces.
Russia already stood accused of leaving "armoured personnel carriers parked recklessly near the reactors" ( Daily Mail ) before they tried parking them inside the houses the reactors lived in.
Alleged Attacks from the Russian-Occupied ZNPP Back on March 4, terrible questions were raised in some minds.

The New York Times would report "The Russians have been firing from the cover of the Zaporizhzhia station since mid-July, Ukrainian military and civilian officials said, sending rockets over the river at Nikopol and other targets." The reason seems to be the increasing use of long-range HIMARS missiles that made other firing spots too vulnerable.
It was on July 16 that Petro Kotin, the President of “Energoatom” (the utility that runs the ZNPP) reported "The Russians have been controlling Zaporizhzhia NPP since the beginning of March.
One "expert" on Russian evils, Luke Harding, advertised the video & report as "showing a #Russian multiple rocket launcher firing from the territory of Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant.
Otherwise Kiev says they were just watching, in terrified awe, as the Russians launched attacks from the plant and then shelled themselves in return, over and over.

These have been mostly blamed on the Russians, but that's always been illogical, and the evidence seems to disagree; some attacks were done by kamikaze drone like in that July attack, and some were by artillery or rockets shown as fired from Ukrainian areas, despite Ukrainian claims ( August 6 from the northwest, August 27 from the northwest or north).

As a result of these attacks, there are casualties and injuries among the employees of the nuclear power plant and residents of the city." International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi would say on September 9.
but on the 20th, Russian-affiliated sources reported another attack .
So far, it might be that Russian artillery and rockets - wherever they're fired from - are the only tools willing and able to stop the attacks, if only for a moment.

The Site that Asks: Is the "dictator" justifying intervention by killing innocents?
Wednesday, September 21, 2022 The "Militarization" of the ZNPP, Part 2: Russian Shelling FROM ZNPP?
Part one, The Battle of March 4 , was originally included with this, but it seemed tedious that way, so I gave that its own post.
In summary: Russian tried to force their way into the plant in the early hours of March 4.
This resistance stopped the Russian takeover about as much as a peaceful surrender would have.
But along with the Russians came a new and dreadful reality: the ZNPP would be occupied by military units who might put it at risk.

I'll start with Statement by Mikhail Ulyanov, 15 September 2022 - Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation (mid.ru) : "In this hall, there have already been calls for the "demilitarization of the ZNPP" or the creation of a kind of "demilitarized perimeter" around it.
It was framed as dangerous and unacceptable on the Russian end, and Ukraine could be faulted for nothing.
Later, the "assigned military unit" would be Russian, not Ukrainian.
The place had suddenly been "militarized." They may not be sparking battles inside the plant, like Ukraine's garrison did, but they allegedly launched shelling attacks from there.
Only equipment for the transportation of Rosgvardia personnel and electronic warfare equipment that helps neutralize Ukrainian drones.
Thus, there were and are no military targets that could serve as a pretext for justifying Ukrainian shelling and attacks on the station." But of course Ukrainian sources tell it differently.

"[O]ver the past three weeks" since early July, "the Russian military has parked Grad multiple rocket launchers between the reactor buildings, to protect them from retaliatory strikes." But the visual record can only support a single Grad launcher between the outer spray ponds.
